name: Ultra Water (three.js FFT ocean renderer)
summary: Open-source real-time ocean renderer for three.js (WebGL2) with a demo island scene: Tessendorf FFT waves (4 cascades), shore breakers on an eikonal travel-time field, textured crest foam, caustics, planar reflections, underwater view and floating props (buoyancy). Author benchmark: ~208–303 fps on an RTX 3060 at 3.3 MP; mobile profile holds 60 fps on a Snapdragon 7+ Gen 3.

access.notes: MIT: keep the copyright notice. Source code only (no npm package); runs from the repo with Vite.

procedure: Open https://github.com/Humpalumps/Ultra-Water and download the master zip (or git clone).
Run npm install, then npm run dev.
Open the printed localhost URL; pick shots from the camera dropdown and tweak quality in the settings panel.
Reuse src/water/OceanSim.js and OceanSurface.js in your own three.js scene.

verdict.why: Rare, production-grade open-source ocean for the web: FFT waves, breakers, foam, caustics and underwater at 200+ fps, MIT, no account. 270 stars in a day and 1.4k likes / 1.4k bookmarks on the author's post. Code-only (no prebuilt package).
